question: The matrix $\begin{bmatrix}0&1&-2\\ -1&0&-7\\ 2&7&0\end{bmatrix}$ is a:
explanation:
Step 1 Let us denote the given matrix as $A = \begin{bmatrix}0&1&-2\\ -1&0&-7\\ 2&7&0\end{bmatrix}$. To classify this matrix, we find its transpose $A^T$ by swapping its rows with its columns.

Step 2 Performing the transpose operation gives: $A^T = \begin{bmatrix}0&-1&2\\ 1&0&7\\ -2&-7&0\end{bmatrix}$. Now factor out a scalar negative sign $-1$ from every element inside the transposed matrix.

Step 3 Factoring out the negative gives $-A^T = \begin{bmatrix}0&1&-2\\ -1&0&-7\\ 2&7&0\end{bmatrix} = A \implies A^T = -A$. By definition, any matrix that satisfies $A^T = -A$ is a skew-symmetric matrix. This corresponds to option C.
